title: Upgrade to support OpenMRS Platform 3.0
body:
Updates patientflags so it builds against, and runs on, openmrs-core master (Platform 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT: Java 21, Jakarta EE, Spring 7, Hibernate 7). Same approach as the platform 3 upgrades of calculation (openmrs/openmrs-module-calculation#19), legacyui and webservices.rest. (openmrs/openmrs-module-patientflags#104 targets Platform 2.8; this targets 3.0.)

## Changes
- Versions and build:
  - Module version is now 4.0.0-SNAPSHOT, on Platform 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT (`openmrs-bom` imported), webservices.rest 5.0.0-SNAPSHOT, legacyui 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT and fhir2 6.0.0-SNAPSHOT.
  - Builds with Java 21 and `-parameters`, using compiler 3.15.0, surefire 3.5.4 and lombok 1.18.42. Lombok runs from `annotationProcessorPaths`, which javac 23 and later need, so the Java 25 build works too.
  - The dead openmrs-1.9/1.10/1.11 and "Java 17" profiles are removed.
  - `openmrs-web` comes off the api/fhir test classpath, and Groovy now comes from the BOM.
  - The README's Java prerequisite is now 21 or 25.
- `config.xml` now sets `require_version` to 3.0.0. All optional modules stay aware-of only. `release.yml` uses Java 21.
- REST: all 5 resources add `"3.*"` to `supportedOpenmrsVersions`.
- `HibernateFlagDAO`:
  - Every Criteria/Restrictions/Projections query is now HQL.
  - The `tags` filter is now a join on tag name. The old `Restrictions.in("tags", List<String>)` could not have worked.
  - Lookups by uuid use `getSingleResultOrNull()`.
- hbm `native` generators are now `identity`. On PostgreSQL, Tag's generator used to take its ids from `patientflags_flag_flag_id_seq`, so a new PostgreSQL-only changeset moves the `tag_id` sequence past the existing tags before identity inserts start using it.
- `PatientFlagTask` uses `Daemon.runInDaemonThreadWithoutResult` / `runNewDaemonTask`, since the old Daemon methods were removed from core.
- `FlagServiceImpl`:
  - `evaluateAllFlags()` returns the daemon `Future`, which completes only once every per-flag task has finished. Before, it passed an already-started daemon thread to an executor, so the returned future didn't track that thread's evaluation.
  - `refreshCache()` adds proxy "Get Global Properties" and "Manage Privileges" privileges. Core 3.0 requires them for `getGlobalProperty` and `getAllPrivileges` (called when `patientflags.username` is a superuser, which `admin` is by default), and the Groovy evaluator calls this from an unauthenticated thread.
- `GroovyFlagEvaluatorThread`: fixes a lost-notify race. It used a bare `wait()` with no condition, so it hung forever if the evaluator finished first; the api tests hung on it. It now waits on a `done` flag.
- commons-lang becomes lang3, and `javax.servlet` becomes `jakarta.servlet`.
- fhir:
  - `FhirFlagDaoImpl` is ported to fhir2 6.x's `OpenmrsFhirCriteriaContext` API.
  - The UCUM `constructor-arg` in the fhir jar's context now uses `type="java.io.InputStream"`, matching fhir2 6.x.
- Tests:
  - Migrated to JUnit 5.
  - `PatientFlagTranslatorImplTest`'s fixture now sets the flag's patient, so the subject mapping is exercised and strict stubbing passes.
  - `FlagServiceTest` adds tests for the `searchFlags` tag filter and for building the privilege cache for a superuser with no authenticated user.
  - `FhirFlagServiceImplTest` lets `toFhirResources` call the real method, like fhir2's own tests.
  - The FHIR dataset's flagged patient moves from person 1 (the admin) to a new person 100, with the same name and uuid. Hibernate 7 can't hold Person#1 and Patient#1 in one result.
  - `concept_name_tag_map` rows are dropped, since that table has no primary key in the test schema.

## Verification
- `mvn clean package` passes on Java 21 and 25: api 83, fhir 30.
- The PostgreSQL changeset was run with Liquibase 4.32.0 on PostgreSQL 16.15, against tags seeded the way the 2.x generator wrote them. Without it, new tags hit duplicate keys; with it, they continue after the highest existing id. Other databases skip it.
- I deployed the omod on openmrs-core master (`mvn jet

title: Separate OWASP dependency check into its own job
body:
## Summary
- Separate OWASP dependency check into a standalone workflow job
- OWASP check only runs on push and workflow_dispatch (not on PRs)
- Build job no longer runs the OWASP check inline or needs the NVD_API_KEY secret

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify build job still passes
- [ ] Verify OWASP dependency check runs on push to the default branch
- [ ] Verify OWASP dependency check does not run on pull requests
